dimensions.assessment: Affects United States nationals or lawful permanent residents who have been wrongfully detained abroad, their next of kin, and journalists or individuals meeting exception criteria.
dimensions.evidence: eligible United States national means-- (i) a national of the United States or lawful permanent resident who has been unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad

dimensions.assessment: Provides direct financial compensation based on average wages and days detained, treated as damages for human suffering, which is a significant, life-changing effect for affected individuals.
dimensions.evidence: the amount described shall be the amount equal to the product of-- (i) the average wage index divided by 365; and (ii) the number of days detained

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations of such sums as may be necessary from unobligated balances of the Department of Justice Assets Forfeiture Fund.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this subsection such sums as may be necessary

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Robert Levinson Hostage Recovery and Hostage-taking Accountability Act to establish a new compensation program, application procedures, public awareness campaigns, and rules regarding tax treatment and means-tested programs.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of State shall compensate an eligible United States national in the amount described under paragraph (3).

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent program structure for eligible individuals to apply after release or death, resulting in one-time lump sum payments.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of State shall make a one time, lump sum payment to an eligible United States national.

missing_information: Total expected cost or exact dollar amounts for appropriations are not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates a compensation and reintegration program for unlawfully or wrongfully detained United States nationals or their next of kin, funded from unobligated balances of the Department of Justice Assets Forfeiture Fund.
